newsitem.title: USA: Avon Q1 sales in U.S. down 1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Avon Q1 sales in U.S. down 1 percent.

text.p: Avon Products Inc said on Wednesday that its first-quarter sales in the United States market -- its biggest -- were down one percent from a year ago, and pretax profits were down two percent.
Overall, Avon reported net income per share of $0.31 compared to $0.28 a year ago, helped by strong performances in Europe, the Pacific region and Mexico.
Excluding the recently acquired Discovery Toys unit, which had a small loss, Avon's U.S. sales for the quarter were down two percent, but pretax profits were up two percent.

U.S. sales of jewelry and accessories and home entertainment products were down significantly due in part to a change in the pricing of "demonstration products" sold to sales representatives, the company said.
Pacific region sales rose almost 20 percent, with gains in all markets except Japan, hurt by currency translation.
Avon Japan did have double-digit sales increase in local currency, its first quarterly increase in two years. Profits are expected to improve later in the year, the company said.
European sales were especially strong in the United Kingdom and the emerging markets of Eastern Europe. Mexico had double-digit profit growth.
